title: حِكَايَةُ الشَّاهِدِ
titleEn: The Steward's Tale: the Young Man with the Severed Thumbs, and the Lady in the Chest
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 217–223 (Night 27, continuing directly from nights-26), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 27 opens as the King of China is about to hang the Christian, the Jew, the physician and the tailor. The steward (الشاهد) steps forward and asks leave to tell a stranger tale. He tells of a dinner at which a young man would not touch the zīr-bāja until he had washed his hands a hundred and twenty times; when he finally ate, the company saw that his thumbs were cut off. Asked why, the young man begins his story: a merchant's son in Baghdad in the days of Hārūn al-Rashīd, he fell in love with a lady who came to his shop, and she, a favourite of Lady Zubayda, smuggled him into the caliph's palace in a chest. The night ends as the Caliph orders the chests opened and the young man recites the confession of faith. Verse is copied as printed. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some of the Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّابِعَةُ وَالْعِشْرُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sābiʿatu wa-al-ʿishrūna
sentences.l: So when it was the night, the seventh and the twenty
sentences.i: And when it was the twenty-seventh night,
sentences.n: The night formula. 'Night' takes the feminine ordinal; the nominative -ūna on the tens is as printed.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أنَّ مَلِكَ الصِّينِ لَمَّا قَالَ لَابُدَّ مِنْ شَنْقِكُمْ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna malika al-ṣīni lammā qāla lābudda min shanqikum
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the fortunate, that the king of China, when he said, 'There-is-no-escape from your hanging,'
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when the king of China said, 'You must all be hanged,'
sentences.n: Shahrazād speaks. The formula 'balaghanī ayyuhā al-malik al-saʿīd' opens each night's resumption. lābudda is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ تَقَدَّمَ الشَّاهِدُ لِمَلِكِ الصِّينِ وَقَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika taqaddama al-shāhidu li-maliki al-ṣīni wa-qāla
sentences.l: then at that, the witness came-forward to the king of China and said,
sentences.i: at that, the witness stepped forward to the king of China and said,
sentences.n: al-shāhid is printed so; it can mean a court witness or notary. Possibly a corruption of another title, but the printed word is kept.

sentences.t: إنْ أذِنْتَ لِى حَكَيْتُ لَكَ حِكَايَةً اتَّفَقَتْ لِى فِي تِلْكَ الْمُدَّةِ قَبْلَ أنْ أجِدَ هَذَا الْأحْدَبَ
sentences.tr: in aʾdhinta lī ḥakaytu laka ḥikāyatan ittafaqat lī fī tilka al-muddati qabla an ajida hādhā al-aḥdaba
sentences.l: If you permit me, I will-relate to you a tale that-befell me in that time before I found this hunchback,
sentences.i: If you permit me, I shall tell you a tale that befell me some time before I found this hunchback,
sentences.n: The perfect ḥakaytu in the apodosis ('I will tell') is a standard way of stating a conditional promise.

sentences.t: وَإنْ كَانَتْ أعْجَبَ مِنْ حَدِيثِهِ تَهَبُ لَنَا أرْوَاحَنَا
sentences.tr: wa-in kānat aʿjaba min ḥadīthihi tahabu lanā arwāḥanā
sentences.l: and if it is more-wondrous than his speech, you-grant to-us our spirits.
sentences.i: and if it is more wondrous than his story, you will grant us our lives.
sentences.n: Classical would put the apodosis verb in the jussive (tahab); the print gives an unmarked form, read here as indicative. The 'spirits' (arwāḥ) are the lives of the condemned.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَلِكُ نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-maliku naʿam
sentences.l: So the king said, 'Yes.'
sentences.i: The king said, 'Yes.'

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أعْلَمْ أنِّي كُنْتُ فِى اللَّيْلَةِ الْمَاضِيَةِ عِنْدَ جَمَاعَةٍ عَمِلُوا خَتْمَةً وَجَمَعُوا أفُقَهَاءَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla iʿlam annī kuntu fī al-laylati al-māḍiyati ʿinda jamāʿatin ʿamilū khatmatan wa-jamaʿū afuqahāʾa
sentences.l: So he said: Know that I was in the night the passed, at a company who made a completion, and they gathered jurists,
sentences.i: He said: Know that last night I was with a company who held a khatma, and they had gathered jurists,
sentences.n: khatma is a gathering to complete a recitation of the Qurʾān. The printed افقهاء has a stray initial alif; it is probably a slip for al-fuqahāʾ ('the jurists') and is read so, with the alif left as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَرَأَ الْمُقْرِئُونَ وَفَرَغُوا مُدَّ السِّمَاطُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qaraʾa al-muqriʾūna wa-faraghū muddā al-simāṭu
sentences.l: So when the reciters had-recited and finished, the spread was extended,
sentences.i: When the reciters had recited and finished, the table-cloth was spread,
sentences.n: The precomposed hamza on qaraʾa and muqriʾūn is the edition's own. The passive mudda ('was stretched out') describes laying the meal.

sentences.t: فَمِنْ جُمْلَةِ مَا قَدَّمُوا زِيرْبَاجَةً
sentences.tr: fa-min jumlati mā qaddamū zīrbājatan
sentences.l: and among the sum of what they presented was a zīrbāja,
sentences.i: and among all they set out was a zirbaja,
sentences.n: zīrbāja is a dish of meat in a sweet-and-sour sauce, the standard Persian-derived name.

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمْنَا نَأكُلُ مِنَ الزِّيرْ بَاجَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddamnā naʾkulu mina al-zīr bājati
sentences.l: so we came-forward, we-eat from the zīr-bāja,
sentences.i: so we came forward to eat of the zirbaja,
sentences.n: naʾkulu follows taqaddamnā without 'to': an asyndetic verb pair, common in Middle Arabic. The dish name is split in two words here.

sentences.t: فَتَأخَّرَ وَاحِدٌمِنَّا وَامْتَنَعَ مِنَ الْأكْلِ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-taʾakhkhara wāḥidunminnā wa-imtanaʿa mina al-akli minhā
sentences.l: but there-held-back one-of-us and refrained from the eating of it,
sentences.i: but one of our number held back and refused to eat of it,
sentences.n: wāḥidunminnā is printed as a single word, 'one of us'.

sentences.t: فَحَلَفْنَا عَلَيْهِ فَأقْسَمَ هُوَ أنْ لَايَأكُلَ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ḥalafnā ʿalayhi fa-aqsama huwa an lāyaʾkula minhā
sentences.l: so we swore upon him, and he swore that he-would-not eat of it,
sentences.i: We adjured him, but he swore he would never eat of it,
sentences.n: ḥalafa ʿalā means to adjure someone by oath. lāyaʾkula is printed as one word; the subjunctive after an is read as Classical.

sentences.t: فَألْزَمْنَاهُ فَقَالَ لَا تَغْصِبُونِي فَكَفَانِي مَاجَرَى لِى مِنْ أكْلِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-alzamnāhu fa-qāla lā taghṣibūnī fa-kafānī mājarā lī min aklihā
sentences.l: so we pressed-him, and he said: Do not compel me, for sufficient-for-me is what happened to me from the eating of it,
sentences.i: We pressed him hard, but he said, 'Do not force me; what befell me through eating it is enough for me,'
sentences.n: mājarā is printed as one word, 'what happened'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: thumma anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: then he recited, saying,
sentences.i: Then he recited, saying:

sentences.t: خُذْ مِلْيحًا فَوْقَ كَتِفِكَ وَارْتَحِلْ * وَإِنْ يَطِبْ لَكَ ذٰلِكَ اللَّيْلَ اكْتَحِلْ
sentences.tr: khudh milyḥan fawqa katifika wa-irtaḥil * wa-in yaṭib laka dhālika al-layla iktaḥil
sentences.l: Take a handsome-one upon your shoulder and depart, * and if that night is pleasant to you, apply-kohl.
sentences.i: Take a fair one on your shoulder and be gone, and if that night should please you, put on kohl.
sentences.n: The pointing here is the edition’s own. The printed milyḥan (kasra, sukūn) is odd; the sense is a 'handsome' or perhaps 'salted' (malīḥ) thing, and the double meaning is not resolved. dhālika al-layla is an accusative of time, 'on that night'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ قُلْنَا لَهُ بِاللّٰهِ عَلَيْكَ مَا سَبَبُ امْتِنَاعِكَ مِنَ الْأَكْلِ مِنَ الزِّيرْ بَاجَهْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha qulnā lahu bi-Allāhi ʿalayka mā sababu imtināʿika mina al-akli mina al-zīr bājah
sentences.l: And-when he finished, we-said to-him: "By-God upon-you, what (is) the-cause of-your-refraining from the-eating from the-zīr-bāja?"
sentences.i: When he had finished, we said to him, "We beg you by God, what keeps you from eating of the zīr-bāja?"
sentences.n: Zīr-bāja (زيرباج) is a Persian-derived meat dish, a sweet-and-sour stew; the edition spells the second word with final ه here and ة later. بِاللّٰهِ عَلَيْكَ, literally "by God upon you", is a common formula of adjuration: "I implore you by God."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ إِنْكَانَ وَلَابُدَّأَنْ آكُلَ مِنْ هٰذِهِ الزِّيرْ بَاجَةِ فَلَا آكُلُ مِنْهَا الْآنَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla inkāna wa-lā-budda-an ākula min hādhihi al-zīr bājati fa-lā ākulu minhā al-āna
sentences.l: And-he-said: "If-it-be, and no-avoiding that I-eat from this the-zīr-bāja, then I-eat-not from-it now
sentences.i: He said, "If I must eat of this zīr-bāja, then I will not eat of it just yet;
sentences.n: Note the printed word-gluing (انكان, ولابدان) and that zīr-bāja is treated as feminine (هذه). The sentence is left open: what follows says what must be done first.

sentences.t: أَغْسِلُ يَدَيَّ أَرْبَعِينَ مَرَّةً بِالصَّابُونِ وَأَرْبَعِينَ مَرَّةً بِالْأُشْنَانِ وَأَرْبَعِينَ مَرَّةً بِالسُّعْدِ جُمْلَتُهُمْ مِائَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ مَرَّةً
sentences.tr: aghsilu yadayya arbaʿīna marratan bi-al-ṣābūni wa-arbaʿīna marratan bi-al-ushnāni wa-arbaʿīna marratan bi-al-suʿdi jumlatuhum miʾatun wa-ʿishrūna marratan
sentences.l: I-wash my-two-hands forty times with-the-soap, and-forty times with-the-potash, and-forty times with-the-cyperus; their-sum a-hundred and-twenty times."
sentences.i: I must first wash my hands forty times with soap, forty with potash, and forty with sedge-root: a hundred and twenty washings in all."
sentences.n: The text has no "until" or "unless" between this and the previous clause; read the plain present أَغْسِلُ as "I (first) wash". الأشنان (ushnān) is potash or saltwort ash, a cleansing agent; السعد (suʿd) is the sweet-smelling cyperus (sedge) root.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذٰلِكَ أَمَرَ صَاحِبُ الدَّعْوَةِ غِلْمَانَهُ فَأَتَوْا بِالْمَاءِ وَبِالَّذِي طَلَبَهُ فَغَسَلَ يَدَيْهِ كَمَا ذَكَرْنَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika amara ṣāḥibu al-daʿwati ghilmānahu fa-atawā bi-al-māʾi wa-bi-alladhī ṭalabahu fa-ghasala yadayhi kamā dhakarnā
sentences.l: And-at that, commanded the-owner of-the-invitation his-boys, and-they-came with-the-water and-with-that-which he-asked-for-it, and-he-washed his-two-hands as we-mentioned.
sentences.i: At that, the host commanded his servants, and they brought the water and all that he had asked for, and he washed his hands as we have told.

sentences.t: وَجَاءَ الشَّابُّ وَهُوَ مُتَكَرِّهٌ وَجَلَسَ وَمَدَّيَدَةُ وَهُوَ مِثْلُ الْخَائِفِ وَغَمَسَ يَدَةُ فِى الزِّيرْ بَاجَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-jāʾa al-shābbu wa-huwa mutakarrihun wa-jalasa wa-madda-yadahu wa-huwa mithlu al-khāʾifi wa-ghamasa yadahu fī al-zīr bājati
sentences.l: And-came the-youth, and-he reluctant, and-sat, and-stretched-out-his-hand, and-he like the-fearful-one, and-dipped his-hand in the-zīr-bāja.
sentences.i: Then the young man came, unwilling, and sat down and stretched out his hand like one in fear, and dipped it into the zīr-bāja.
sentences.n: The edition regularly spells the pronoun -hu (his) with ة, as in يَدَةُ "his hand"; it is the same pronoun as ـه, so read yadahu. Here ومديدة is printed as one word, wa-madda yadahu.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ يَأْكُلُ وَهُوَ مُتَغَصِّبٌ وَنَحْنُ نَتَعَجَّبُ مِنْهُ غَايَةَ الْعَجَبِ وَيَدُةُ تَرْتَعِدُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra yaʾkulu wa-huwa mutaghaṣṣibun wa-naḥnu nataʿajjabu minhu ghāyata al-ʿajabi wa-yaduhu tartaʿidu
sentences.l: And-he-became eating, and-he forcing-himself, and-we marvelling at-him (to) the-utmost of-the-wonder, and-his-hand trembling.
sentences.i: And he went on eating, forcing himself, while we marvelled at him beyond measure, and his hand shook.
sentences.n: مُتَغَصِّب is obscure. Two candidates: from غَصَبَ "to take by force", so "compelling himself"; or a slip for مُتَغَصِّص, "choking, swallowing with pain" (from غُصَّة). Either way the picture is of a man eating under constraint.

sentences.t: فَنَصَبَ إِبْهَامَ يَدِةِ فَإِذَا هُوَ مَقْطُوعٌ وَهُوَ يَأْكُلُ بِأَرْبَعِ أَصَابِعَ
sentences.tr: fa-naṣaba ibhāma yadihi fa-idhā huwa maqṭūʿun wa-huwa yaʾkulu bi-arbaʿi aṣābiʿa
sentences.l: And-he-set-up the-thumb of-his-hand, and-behold, it (is) cut-off, and-he eating with four fingers.
sentences.i: He raised his thumb, and behold, it was cut off, and he was eating with four fingers.
sentences.n: فَإِذَا هُوَ introduces what is suddenly seen: "and behold".

sentences.t: فَقُلْنَا لَهُ بِاللّٰهِ عَلَيْكَ مَالِإِبْهَا مِكَ هٰكَذَا هُوَ خِلْقَةُ اللّٰهِ أَمْ أَصَابَهُ حَادِثٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qulnā lahu bi-Allāhi ʿalayka mā-li-ibhā mika hākadhā huwa khilqatu Allāhi am aṣābahu ḥādithun
sentences.l: And-we-said to-him: "By-God upon-you, what-for-your-thumb (is it) thus? Is-it the-creation of-God, or befell-it an-accident?"
sentences.i: We said to him, "We beg you by God, what is the matter with your thumb? Were you born so, or did some accident befall it?"
sentences.n: The print splits the word: مالابها مك is ما لإبهامك, "what is with your thumb?", with a stray space. خِلْقَةُ اللّٰهِ, "God's creation", means a natural defect from birth.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا إِخْوَانِي وَمَا هُوَ هٰذَا الْإِبْهَامُ وَحْدَةُ وَلٰكِنْ إِبْهَامِي الْأُخْرَى وَرِجْلَايَ الِاثْنَيْنِ وَلٰكِنْ حَتَّى تَرَ وْاثُمَّ كَشَفَ إِبْهَامَ يَدِةِ الْأُخْرَى
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā ikhwānī wa-mā huwa hādhā al-ibhāmu waḥdahu wa-lākin ibhāmī al-ukhrā wa-rijlāya al-ithnayni wa-lākin ḥattā tara wāthumma kashafa ibhāma yadihi al-ukhrā
sentences.l: And-he-said: "O my-brothers, and-what (is) this the-thumb, its-aloneness? But my-thumb the-other, and my-two-feet the-two; but until you-see." Then he-uncovered the-thumb of-his-hand the-other.
sentences.i: He said, "My brothers, it is not this thumb alone: my other thumb is the same, and both my feet. But see for yourselves." Then he uncovered the thumb of his other hand.
sentences.n: Several slips. وحدة is وحده "alone" with the ة-for-ـه spelling. الاثنين is the fixed oblique dual, used where Classical would say الاثنتان (feminine). In تر واثم the print has moved an alif: read together as تَرَوْا ثُمَّ, "you see; then" (my reconstruction; the print is not clear).

sentences.t: فَوَجَدْنَاهُ مِثْلَ الْيَمِينِ وَكَذٰلِكَ رِجْلَاهُ بِلَا إِبْهَامَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-wajadnāhu mithla al-yamīni wa-kadhālika rijlāhu bi-lā ibhāmayni
sentences.l: And-we-found-it like the-right, and-likewise his-two-feet without two-thumbs.
sentences.i: We found it like the right one, and likewise his feet were without big toes.
sentences.n: إبهام means both "thumb" and "big toe".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَيْنَاهُ كَذٰلِكَ ازْدَدْنَا عَجَبًا وَقُلْنَا لَهُ مَا بَقِيَ لَنَا صَبْرٌ عَلَى حَدِيثِكَ وَسَبَبِ قَطْعِ إِبْهَامَيْكَ وَسَبَبِ غَسْلِ يَدَيْكَ مِائَةً وَعِشْرِينَ مَرَّةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾaynāhu kadhālika izdadnā ʿajaban wa-qulnā lahu mā baqiya lanā ṣabrun ʿalā ḥadīthika wa-sababi qaṭʿi ibhāmayka wa-sababi ghasli yadayka miʾatan wa-ʿishrīna marratan
sentences.l: And-when we-saw-him thus, we-increased (in) wonder; and-we-said to-him: "There-remains not to-us patience for your-tale and the-cause of-the-cutting of-your-two-thumbs and the-cause of-the-washing of-your-hands a-hundred and-twenty times."
sentences.i: When we saw him so, our wonder only grew, and we said to him, "We have no patience left for your story: the reason your thumbs were cut off, and the reason you wash your hands a hundred and twenty times."
sentences.n: The two genitives وَسَبَبِ ... are governed by عَلَى: patience "for" the tale and "for" the reasons.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ اِعْلَمُوا أَنَّ وَالِدِي كَانَ تَاجِرًا مِنَ التُّجَّارِ الْكِبَارِ وَكَانَ أَكْبَرَ تُجَّارِ مَدِينَةِ بَغْدَادَ عَلَى أَيَّامِ الْخَلِيفَةِ هَارُونَ الرَّشِيدِ وَكَانَ مُولَعًا بِشُرْبِ الْخَمْرِ وَسَمَاعِ الْعُودِ وَآلَاتِ الْمَلَاهِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla iʿlamū anna wālidī kāna tājiran mina al-tujjāri al-kibāri wa-kāna akbara tujjāri madīnati Baghdāda ʿalā ayyāmi al-khalīfati Hārūna al-Rashīdi wa-kāna mūlaʿan bi-shurbi al-khamri wa-samāʿi al-ʿūdi wa-ālāti al-malāhī
sentences.l: And-he-said: "Know that my-father was a-merchant from the-merchants the-great-ones, and-was the-greatest of-merchants of-the-city of-Baghdad in the-days of-the-caliph Hārūn al-Rashīd, and-was fond with-the-drinking of-the-wine and-the-hearing of-the-lute and-the-instruments of-the-amusements.
sentences.i: He said, "Know that my father was one of the great merchants, the greatest merchant in the city of Baghdad in the days of the Caliph Hārūn al-Rashīd. He was fond of drinking wine, of listening to the lute, and of the instruments of revelry.
sentences.n: مُولَع ("devoted, passionately fond") takes بِـ for its object. عَلَى أَيَّامِ means "in the days of".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا مَاتَ لَمْ يَتْرُكْ شَيْئًا فَهَيَّأْتُهُ وَقَدْ عَمِلْتُ لَهُ خَتْمَاتٍ وَحَزِنْتُ عَلَيْهِ أَيَّامًا وَلَيَالِيَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā māta lam yatruk shayʾan fa-hayyaʾtuhu wa-qad ʿamiltu lahu khatmātin wa-ḥazintu ʿalayhi ayyāman wa-layāliya
sentences.l: And-when he-died, he-left not anything; so-I-prepared-him, and-indeed I-made for-him whole-Qurʾān-recitals, and-I-grieved over-him days and-nights.
sentences.i: When he died he left nothing to speak of. I prepared him for burial, and had the Qurʾān recited through for him, and mourned him for days and nights.
sentences.n: فهياته is فَهَيَّأْتُهُ, "I made him ready" (washed and shrouded him); the print omits the hamza. ختمات are complete recitations of the Qurʾān held for the dead. "Left nothing" is softened by the next sentence, which finds a little.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ فَتَحْتُ دُكَّانَهُ فَمَا وَجَدْتُهُ خَلَّفَ إِلَّايَسِيرًا وَوَجَدْتُ عَلَيْهِ دُيُونًا فَصَبَّرْتُ أَصْحَابَ الدُّيُونِ وَطَيَّبْتُ خَوَاطِرَهُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma fataḥtu dukkānahu fa-mā wajadtuhu khallafa illā-yasīran wa-wajadtu ʿalayhi duyūnan fa-ṣabbartu aṣḥāba al-duyūni wa-ṭayyabtu khawāṭirahum
sentences.l: Then I-opened his-shop, and-I-found-him not (to have) left except a-little; and-I-found upon-him debts; so-I-made-patient the-owners of-the-debts and-sweetened their-minds.
sentences.i: Then I opened his shop and found that he had left only a trifle, and that he owed debts. So I asked the creditors for patience and set their minds at ease.
sentences.n: The print runs خلف إلا يسيرا together (illā yasīran, "except a little"). طَيَّبَ خَاطِرَهُ is a stock phrase, "to soothe, to put someone's mind at ease".

sentences.t: وَصِرْتُ أَبِيعُ وَأَشْتَرِي مِنَ الْجُمْعَةِ إِلَى الْجُمْعَةِ وَأُعْطِي أَصْحَابَ الدُّيُونِ وَلَا زِلْتُ عَلَى هٰذِهِ الْحَالَةِ مُدَّةً إِلَى أَنْ وَفَّيْتُ الدُّيُونَ وَزِدْتُ عَلَى رَأْسِ مَالِي أَيَّامًا وَلَيَالِيَ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣirtu abīʿu wa-ashtarī mina al-jumʿati ilā al-jumʿati wa-uʿṭī aṣḥāba al-duyūni wa-lā ziltu ʿalā hādhihi al-ḥālati muddatan ilā an waffaytu al-duyūna wa-zidtu ʿalā raʾsi mālī ayyāman wa-layāliya
sentences.l: And-I-became (one who) sells and-buys from-the-Friday to-the-Friday, and-gives the-owners of-the-debts; and-I-ceased-not upon this the-state (for) a-while, until I-paid-in-full the-debts, and-I-added upon the-head of-my-wealth days and-nights.
sentences.i: I took to buying and selling, week after week, and paying the creditors, and I carried on so for a time, until I had paid off the debts and added to my capital, over days and nights.
sentences.n: مِنَ الْجُمْعَةِ إِلَى الْجُمْعَةِ, "from Friday to Friday", means week by week. وَلَا زِلْتُ uses لَا where Classical writes مَا زِلْتُ, "I kept on" (Middle Arabic). رَأْسُ الْمَالِ is "capital".

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا أَنَا فِي يَوْمٍ مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ جَالِسٌ فَمَا أَدْرِي إِلَّاوَصَبِيَّةٌ لَمْ تَرَعَيْنِي أَحْسَنَ مِنْهَا عَلَيْهَا حُلِيٌّ وَحُلَلٌ رَاكِبَةً بَغْلَةً وَقَدْ أَمَّهَا عَبْدٌ وَوَرَاءَهَا عَبْدٌ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā anā fī yawmin mina al-ayyāmi jālisun fa-mā adrī illā-wa-ṣabiyyatun lam tara-ʿaynī aḥsana minhā ʿalayhā ḥuliyyun wa-ḥulalun rākibatan baghlatan wa-qad ammahā ʿabdun wa-warāʾahā ʿabdun
sentences.l: And-while I (was) in a-day of the-days sitting, then I-know not but-and a-girl, my-eye-had-not-seen (any) more-beautiful than-her; upon-her jewels and-robes; riding a-mule; and-indeed had-gone-before-her a-slave and-behind-her a-slave.
sentences.i: One day, as I sat there, suddenly, before I knew it, there appeared a girl, lovelier than any my eyes had ever seen, in jewels and fine robes, riding a mule, with one slave going before her and another behind.
sentences.n: فَمَا أَدْرِي إِلَّا وَ... "I knew nothing until suddenly..." is a stock way of saying "all at once". The print runs together إلا وصبية and لم تر عيني. أَمَّهَا means "went before her", leading the way. رَاكِبَةً is an accusative circumstantial, "riding"; the ة is the printed ending.

sentences.t: فَا وَقَفَتِ الْبَغْلَةُ عَلَى رَأْسِ الْقَيْصَرِيَّةِ وَدَخَلَتْ وَدَخَلَ خَادِمٌ خَلْفَهَا
sentences.tr: fā waqafati al-baghlatu ʿalā raʾsi al-qayṣariyyati wa-dakhalat wa-dakhala khādimun khalfahā
sentences.l: And the-mule stopped at the-head of-the-qayṣariyya, and-she-entered, and-entered a-servant behind-her.
sentences.i: The mule halted at the entrance of the market-hall, and she went in, and a servant went in behind her.
sentences.n: The print has a stray alif and space in فا وقفت. I read it as "and the mule stood still"; fa-awqafat, "she halted the mule", is also possible. القيصرية (qayṣariyya) is a covered market hall of shops. خادم in these tales is regularly a eunuch.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ يَا سِتِّي اُخْرُجِي وَلَا تُعْلِمِي أَحَدًا فَتُطْلِقِي فِينَا النَّارَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla yā sittī ukhrujī wa-lā tuʿlimī aḥadan fa-tuṭliqī fīnā al-nāra
sentences.l: And-he-said: "O my-lady, go-out, and-do-not inform anyone, lest you-let-loose among-us the-fire."
sentences.i: He said, "My lady, go forward, and let no one know of it, or you will set a fire loose among us."
sentences.n: سِتِّي is a contraction of سَيِّدَتِي, "my lady". "To let loose fire among us" means to stir up trouble and scandal.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَجَبَهَا الْخَادِمُ حَتَّى نَظَرَتْ إِلَى دَكَاكِينِ التُّجَّارِ فَلَمْ تَجِدْ أَحَدًا فَتَحَ دُكَّانَهُ غَيْرِي فَتَمَشَّتْ وَالْخَادِمُ خَلْفَهَا وَجَلَسَتْ عَلَى دُكَّانِي وَسَلَّمَتْ عَلَيَّ فَمَا سَمِعْتُ أَحْسَنَ مِنْ حَدِيثِهَا وَلَا أَعْذَبَ مِنْ كَلَامِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma ḥajabahā al-khādimu ḥattā naẓarat ilā dakākīni al-tujjāri fa-lam tajid aḥadan fataḥa dukkānahu ghayrī fa-tamashshat wa-al-khādimu khalfahā wa-jalasat ʿalā dukkānī wa-sallamat ʿalayya fa-mā samiʿtu aḥsana min ḥadīthihā wa-lā aʿdhaba min kalāmihā
sentences.l: Then screened-her the-servant until she-looked at the-shops of-the-merchants, and-she-found not anyone (who) had-opened his-shop other-than-me; so-she-walked-along, and-the-servant behind-her, and-sat upon my-shop, and-greeted upon-me; and-I-heard not (anything) more-beautiful than her-talk, nor sweeter than her-speech.
sentences.i: Then the servant shielded her from view while she looked over the merchants' shops, and she found no one with his shop open but me. So she walked over, the eunuch behind her, and sat at my stall and greeted me; and I never heard talk more beautiful than hers, nor speech sweeter.
sentences.n: حَجَبَهَا is "screened her" (stood so that no one could see her). دُكَّان is a shop, the raised stall-front where the merchant sits.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ كَشَفَتْ عَنْ وَجْهِهَا فَرَأَيْتُهَا مِثْلَ الْقَمَرِ فَنَظَرْتُ لَهَا نَظْرَةً أَعْقَبَتْنِي أَلْفَ حَسْرَةٍ وَتَعَلَّقَ قَلْبِي بِمَحَبَّتِهَا وَجَعَلْتُ أُكَرِّرُ النَّظَرَ إِلَى وَجْهِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma kashafat ʿan wajhihā fa-raʾaytuhā mithla al-qamari fa-naẓartu lahā naẓratan aʿqabatnī alfa ḥasratin wa-taʿallaqa qalbī bi-maḥabbatihā wa-jaʿaltu ukarriru al-naẓara ilā wajhihā
sentences.l: Then she-uncovered from her-face, and-I-saw-her like the-moon; and-I-looked at-her a-look (that) it-left-me-after (it) a-thousand regrets; and-clung my-heart with-love-of-her; and-I-began (to) repeat the-looking to her-face.
sentences.i: Then she uncovered her face, and I saw her, like the moon. I gave her one look that cost me a thousand sighs, and my heart clung to love of her, and I kept gazing again and again at her face.
sentences.n: أَعْقَبَتْنِي أَلْفَ حَسْرَةٍ means the look "left me, as its sequel, a thousand regrets".

sentences.t: وَأَنْشَدْتُ أَقُولُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-anshadtu aqūlu shiʿrun
sentences.l: And-I-recited, saying: verse.
sentences.i: Then I recited these verses.
sentences.n: The slice ends on this lead-in; the verses themselves follow.

sentences.t:
قُلْ لِلْمَلِيحَةِ فِي الْخِمَارِ الْفَاخِتِي * اَلْمَوْتُ حَقًّا مِنْ عَذَابِكِ رَاحَتِي
جُودِي بِوَصْلٍ عَلَّنِي اُحْيَى بِهِ * هَا قَدْ مَدَدْتُ اِلَى نَوَالِكِ رَاحَتِي
sentences.tr:
qul li-al-malīḥa fī al-khimāri al-fākhitī * al-mawtu ḥaqqan min ʿadhābiki rāḥatī
jūdī bi-waṣlin ʿallanī uḥyā bi-hi * hā qad madadtu ilā nawāliki rāḥatī
sentences.l: Say to-the-fair-one in the-veil the-dove-grey: the-death, truly, from your-torment, (is) my-rest. / Be-generous with-union, perhaps I-be-made-to-live by-it; here, I-have-stretched-out to your-bounty my-palm.
sentences.i: Say to the fair one in the dove-grey veil: truly, death is my rest from your torment. Be generous with your company, that I may live by it; see, I have stretched out my palm to your bounty.
sentences.n: The two lines end on the same word, rāḥatī, in two senses: 'my rest' (relief) in the first, 'my palm' (the open hand held out for a gift) in the second. The pointing here is the edition's own. The ending -ī of al-fākhitī (for al-fākhitiyy) is as printed, for the rhyme.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ مِتِي هَٰذَا الشِّعْرَ أَحَابَتْنِي وَهِيَ تَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat mitī hādhā al-shiʿra aḥābatnī wa-hiya taqūlu
sentences.l: And-when she-heard — mitī — this the-poem, she-answered-me, and-she saying.
sentences.i: When she heard this poem from me, she answered me, saying:
sentences.n: Two printing slips, apparently. The print has متي (mtī), which makes no sense here; مني, minnī, 'from me', is almost certainly meant, and the idiomatic line follows that, but the word is vocalised as printed. احابتني, with ح, is for أجابتني, 'she answered me'.

sentences.t:
عَلِمْتُ اصْطِبَارِي فِي الْهَوَى اَسْلَاكُمُ * وَاِنَّ فُؤَادِي لَا يُحِبُّ سِوَاكُمُ
وَان نَظَرَتْ عَيْنِي اِلَى غَيْرِ حُسْنِكُمْ * فَلَا سَرَّهَا بَعْدَ الْبِعَادِ لِقَاكُمُ
حَلَفْتُ يَمِينًا لَسْتُ اَسْلَا هَوَاكُمُ * وَقَلْبِي حَزِينٌ مُعْجَبٌ بِلِقَاكُمُ
سَقَانِي الْهَوَى كَاسًا مِنَ الْحُبِّ مُتْرَعًا * فَيَالَيْتَهُ لَمَّا سَقَانِي سَقَاكُمُ
خُذُوا الْجِسْمَ مِنِّي مَعَكُمْ اَيْنَ سِرْتُمُ * وَاَيْنَ حَلَلْتُمْ فَادْفِنُونِي حِذَاكُمُ
وَنَادُوا بِاسْمِي عِنْدَ قَبْرِي يُجِيبَكُمْ * اَنِينُ عِظَامِي عِنْدَ وَقْعِ نِدَاكُمُ
فَلَوْقِيلَ لِي مَاذَا عَلَى اللهِ تَشْتَهِي * لَقُلْتُ رِضَى الرَّحْمَنِ ثُمَّ رِضَاكُمُ
sentences.tr:
ʿalimtu iṣṭibārī fī al-hawā aslākumu * wa-inna fuʾādī lā yuḥibbu siwākumu
wa-in naẓarat ʿaynī ilā ghayri ḥusnikum * fa-lā sarrahā baʿda al-biʿādi liqākumu
ḥalaftu yamīnan lastu aslā hawākumu * wa-qalbī ḥazīnun muʿjabun bi-liqākumu
saqānī al-hawā kāsan mina al-ḥubbi mutraʿan * fa-yā-laytahu lammā saqānī saqākumu
khudhū al-jisma minnī maʿakum ayna sirtumu * wa-ayna ḥalaltum fa-idfinūnī ḥidhākumu
wa-nādū bi-ismī ʿinda qabrī yujībakum * anīnu ʿiẓāmī ʿinda waqʿi nidākumu
fa-lawqīla lī mādhā ʿalā Allāhi tashtahī * la-qultu riḍā al-Raḥmāni thumma riḍākumu
sentences.l:
I-knew my-patience in the-love: I-forget-you. * And-indeed my-heart does-not love other-than-you.
And-if my-eye looks to other-than your-beauty * then may-not please-it, after the-distance, meeting-you.
I-swore an-oath: I-am-not forgetting love-of-you * and-my-heart (is) sad, delighted with-meeting-you.
Love gave-me-to-drink a-cup from the-love, brim-full * so-oh-would-that-it, when it-gave-me-to-drink, had-given-you-to-drink.
Take the-body from-me with-you wherever you-go * and-wherever you-alight, then-bury-me beside-you.
And-call by-my-name at my-grave: it-answers-you * the-groaning of-my-bones at the-falling of-your-call.
So-if-it-were-said to-me, 'What of God do-you-desire?' * I-would-say: the-good-pleasure of-the-Merciful, then your-good-pleasure.
sentences.i:
I knew my patience in love would make me forget you, and yet my heart loves none but you.
If my eye should ever look on any beauty but yours, then after this parting may meeting you never gladden it.
I have sworn an oath that I will not forget my love for you; my heart is sorrowful, yet delighted at the thought of meeting you.
Love gave me to drink a brimming cup of affection; would that, when it gave me to drink, it had given you to drink as well.
Take my body with you wherever you go, and wherever you halt, bury me beside you.
Call out my name beside my grave, and the moaning of my bones will answer you at the sound of your calling.
And if I were asked, "What do you desire of God?" I would say: the good pleasure of the Merciful, and then yours.
sentences.n: The pointing here is the edition's own, copied as printed. The first line is hard: aslākumu is read as 'I forget you' (compare lastu aslā hawākumu in line 3), and the line seems to say 'I tested my patience in love, and I would forget you', followed by a protest that the heart never does; the sense is uncertain. In line 2 the print points only the waw of وَان, leaving the rest bare; it is read wa-in, 'and if'. Final -u on sirtumu, ḥalaltum-style plural endings and the dropped hamza of liqā' and nidā' are as printed, for the rhyme -kumu.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَتْ مِنْ شِعْرِهَا قَالَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghat min shiʿrihā qālat
sentences.l: And-when she-finished from her-poetry, she-said:
sentences.i: When she had finished her verses, she said:

sentences.t: يَافَتًى عِنْدَكَ تَفَاصِيلُ مِلَاحٌ
sentences.tr: yā-fatā ʿindaka tafāṣīlu milāḥun
sentences.l: O-youth, with-you (are) cut-lengths (of cloth), fine-ones.
sentences.i: Young man, have you any fine cloths, cut to length?
sentences.n: Read as a question without a question word; the pitch of the voice carries it. تفاصيل (tafāṣīl) is taken here as cloth cut in pieces or lengths, which suits the shopping that follows. The print joins يا to فتى.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ يَاسِتِّي مَمْلُوكُكِ فَقِيرٌ وَلَكِنِ اصْبِرِي حَتَّى تَفْتَحَ التُّجَّارُ دَكَاكِينَهُمْ وَأَجِيبَ لَكِ مَا تُرِيدِينَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu yā-sittī mamlūkuki faqīrun wa-lākini iṣbirī ḥattā taftaḥa al-tujjāru dakākīnahum wa-ajība laki mā turīdīnahu
sentences.l: And-I-said: O-my-lady, your-slave (is) poor, but be-patient until the-merchants open their-shops and-I-bring for-you what you-want.
sentences.i: I said, "My lady, your servant is a poor man; but be patient until the merchants open their shops, and I will fetch you whatever you desire."
sentences.n: مملوكك, 'your slave', is a polite way of saying 'I'. اجيب is from جاب (jāba), 'bring', a Middle Arabic or colloquial verb (Classical جاء بـ); it is vocalised as Form I, ajību, here subjunctive after حتى. The merchants are plural but take a feminine singular verb (تفتح), a Classical option for broken plurals.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَحَدَّثْتُ أَنَا وَإِيَّاهَا وَأَنَا غَارِقٌ فِي بَحْرِ مَحَبَّتِهَا تَائِهٌ فِي عِشْقِهَا حَتَّى فَتَحَتِ التُّجَّارُ دَكَاكِينَهُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma taḥaddathtu anā wa-iyyāhā wa-anā ghāriqun fī baḥri maḥabbatihā tāʾihun fī ʿishqihā ḥattā fataḥati al-tujjāru dakākīnahum
sentences.l: Then I-conversed, I and-her, while-I (was) drowning in the-sea of-her-love, wandering-lost in her-passion, until the-merchants opened their-shops.
sentences.i: Then she and I talked together, I drowning in the sea of her love and lost in her passion, until the merchants opened their shops.
sentences.n: ثم تحدثت أنا وإياها: 'I and she conversed'. The two participles, drowning and lost, are the narrator's state, a lover's commonplace.

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَأَخَذْتُ لَهَا جَمِيعَ مَا طَلَبَتْهُ وَكَانَ ثَمَنُ ذَٰلِكَ خَمْسَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ وَنَاوَلْتُهُمْ لِلْخَادِمِ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-akhadhtu lahā jamīʿa mā ṭalabathu wa-kāna thamanu dhālika khamsata ālāfi dirhamin wa-nāwaltuhum li-al-khādimi
sentences.l: And-I-rose, and-I-took for-her all (of) what she-requested; and-was the-price of-that five (of) thousands (of) dirham; and-I-handed-them to-the-servant.
sentences.i: I got up and took for her everything she had asked for. The price of it all came to five thousand dirhams, and I handed the goods to the servant.
sentences.n: 'Them' (-hum, masculine plural) stands for the goods, the ordinary pronoun for things in this register.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَهُمُ الْخَادِمُ وَخَرَجُوا إِلَى بَرِّ الْقَيْصَرِيَّةِ فَقَدَّمُوا لَهَا الْبَغْلَةَ فَرَكِبَتْ وَلَمْ تَذْكُرْلِي هِيَ مِنْ أَيْنَ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhahumu al-khādimu wa-kharajū ilā barri al-qayṣariyyati fa-qaddamū lahā al-baghlata fa-rakibat wa-lam tadhkurlī hiya min ayna
sentences.l: And-took-them the-servant, and-they-went-out to the-outside of-the-qayṣariyya; and-they-presented to-her the-mule, and-she-rode; and-she-did-not mention-to-me, she, from where.
sentences.i: The servant took them, and they went out to the edge of the market-hall, where the mule was brought forward for her, and she mounted. She did not tell me where she came from.
sentences.n: القيصرية, al-qayṣariyya, is a covered market hall; barr is the outside or open ground beside it. 'They went out' is plural although only the servant is named: he and her other attendants. The print runs تذكر and لي together.

sentences.t: وَاسْتَحْيَيْتُ أَنِّي أَذْكُرُ لَهَا ذَٰلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-istaḥyaytu annī adhkuru lahā dhālika
sentences.l: And-I-was-ashamed that-I mention to-her that.
sentences.i: And I was ashamed to raise the matter with her.
sentences.n: أني أذكر, 'that I mention', keeps the indicative where Classical would more often use a subjunctive or a verbal noun after a verb of this kind; the idiom is Middle Arabic. 'That' is her origin, which she had not told.

sentences.t: وَالْتَزَمَتِ التُّجَّارُ لِي بِالثَّمَنِ
sentences.tr: wa-iltazamati al-tujjāru lī bi-al-thamani
sentences.l: And-undertook the-merchants for-me (to-answer) for-the-price.
sentences.i: and the merchants took the price upon themselves for me.
sentences.n: التزم, 'bind oneself to', with لي and بالثمن: the merchants committed themselves to the sum on my behalf, apparently letting the payment wait. The exact commercial arrangement is not spelled out.

sentences.t: وَاسْتَلَمْتُ الْغِرَاسَةَ بِخَمْسَةِ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ وَجِئْتُ الْبَيْتَ وَأَنَا سَكْرَانُ مِنْ مَحَبَّتِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-istalamtu al-ghirāsata bi-khamsati ālāfi dirhamin wa-jiʾtu al-bayta wa-anā sakrānu min maḥabbatihā
sentences.l: And-I-took-delivery-of the-ghirāsa for five (of) thousands (of) dirham, and-I-came (to) the-house, and-I (was) drunk from her-love.
sentences.i: I took delivery of the goods for five thousand dirhams, and came home drunk with love of her.
sentences.n: الغراسة is obscure. Taken from غِراس, 'plants, saplings', it would be 'the planting', which hardly fits; it must be the purchased lot. The word may be a misprint, for instance for الكراسة, 'the bundle', but that is only a guess, so the idiomatic line says 'the goods'. جئت البيت takes the house as a direct object, 'I came to the house'.

sentences.t: فَقَٰلَ مَوَالِيَّ الْعَشَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla mawāliyya al-ʿashā
sentences.l: And-said my-masters/people the-supper.
sentences.i: Then my people said, "Supper!"
sentences.n: The print has فقل, which would be فقال with the long vowel unwritten, so it is pointed with a dagger alif. The sentence is nonetheless odd: perhaps فقدّم, 'they served', or a misprint of some other verb. The sense is clearly that supper was called or served. العشا is the print's spelling of العشاء, written with final alif and no hamza.

sentences.t: فَأَكَلْتُ لُقْمَةً وَتَذَكَّرْتُ حُسْنَهَا وَجَمَالَهَا وَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَنَامَ
sentences.tr: fa-akaltu luqmatan wa-tadhakkartu ḥusnahā wa-jamālahā wa-aradtu an anāma
sentences.l: And-I-ate a-morsel, and-I-remembered her-beauty and-her-comeliness, and-I-wanted that I-sleep.
sentences.i: I ate a mouthful, and remembered her beauty and loveliness, and I wanted to sleep.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَجِئْنِي نَوْمٌ وَلَمْ أَزَلْ عَلَى هَٰذِهِ الْحَالَةِ جُمْعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-lam yajiʾnī nawmun wa-lam azal ʿalā hādhihi al-ḥālati jumʿatan
sentences.l: And-not came-to-me sleep, and-I-did-not cease upon this the-state (for) a-week.
sentences.i: but sleep would not come to me, and I remained in this state for a week.
sentences.n: جمعة, jumʿa, means 'week' here (it is also the word for Friday). لم أزل is 'I did not cease', that is, 'I kept on'.

sentences.t: فَطَالَبُونِي التُّجَّارُ بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭālabūnī al-tujjāru bi-amwālihim
sentences.l: so they-pressed-me, the-merchants, for their-monies
sentences.i: Then the merchants pressed me for their money.
sentences.n: The plural verb comes before its subject and a pronoun (-ūnī) anticipates the noun; Classical Arabic would say فطالبني التجار.

sentences.t: فَصَبَّرْتُهُمْ جُمْعَةً أُخْرَى
sentences.tr: fa-ṣabbartuhum jumʿatan ukhrā
sentences.l: so I-made-them-wait a-week another
sentences.i: So I put them off for another week.
sentences.n: جمعة here is a week of seven days (it is also the word for Friday).

sentences.t: فَبَعْدَ الْجُمْعَةِ إِلَّا وَهِيَ أَقْبَلَتْ رَاكِبَةً الْبَغْلَةَ وَمَعَهَا خَادِمٌ وَعَبْدَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-baʿda al-jumʿati illā wa-hiya aqbalat rākibatan al-baghlata wa-maʿahā khādimun wa-ʿabdayni
sentences.l: so after the-week — nothing-but she: she-approached, riding the-mule, and with-her a-servant and two-slaves
sentences.i: And after that week, behold, there she was, coming on her mule, with a servant and two slaves in her train.
sentences.n: إلا وهي after a negative or implied negative (here understood: 'I was unaware') means 'and suddenly she...'. The final وعبدين is oblique where Classical has nominative عبدان, a common Middle Arabic levelling of the dual.

sentences.t: فَسَلَّمَتْ عَلَيَّ وَقَالَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-sallamat ʿalayya wa-qālat
sentences.l: so she-greeted upon-me and she-said
sentences.i: She greeted me and said:

sentences.t: يَا سَيِّدِي أَبْطَأْنَا عَلَيْكَ بِثَمَنِ الْقُمَاشِ
sentences.tr: yā sayyidī abṭaʾnā ʿalayka bi-thamani al-qumāshi
sentences.l: O my-master, we-were-slow upon-you with the-price of-the-cloth
sentences.i: My lord, we have been slow in bringing you the price of the cloth.
sentences.n: أبطأ عليه 'to be slow to someone' takes بـ for the thing delayed.

sentences.t: فَهَاتِ الصَّيْرَفِيَّ وَاقْبِضِ الثَّمَنَ
sentences.tr: fa-hāti al-ṣayrafiyya wa-iqbiḍi al-thamana
sentences.l: so bring the-money-changer and seize the-price
sentences.i: So bring the money-changer, and take the price.

sentences.t: فَجَاءَ الصَّيْرَفِيُّ وَأَخْرَجَ لَهُ الطَّوَاشِيُّ الثَّمَنَ فَقَبَضْتُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-jāʾa al-ṣayrafiyyu wa-akhraja lahu al-ṭawāshiyyu al-thamana fa-qabaḍtuhu
sentences.l: so he-came, the-money-changer, and he-brought-out for-him the-eunuch the-price, and I-seized-it
sentences.i: So the money-changer came, the eunuch counted out the price for him, and I took it.
sentences.n: الطواشي is the eunuch attendant, the same person called الخادم 'servant' above. له 'for him' is unclear: perhaps the money-changer, to weigh it, or a slip for لي 'for me'.

sentences.t: وَصِرْتُ أَتَحَدَّثُ أَنَا وَإِيَّاهَا إِلَى أَنْ فُتِحَ السُّوقُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣirtu ataḥaddathu ana wa-iyyāhā ilā an futiḥa al-sūqu
sentences.l: and I-became I-converse, I and her, until that was-opened the-market
sentences.i: And I sat talking with her until the market opened.
sentences.n: صار + imperfect means 'began, went on'. أنا وإياها 'I and her' uses the object pronoun إيّاها inside a subject phrase, a Middle Arabic habit. The print leaves فتح unpointed; I read it as passive, 'was opened' (the market opened).

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ خُذْلِي كَذَا وَكَذَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat khudhlī kadhā wa-kadhā
sentences.l: so she-said: take-for-me such and such
sentences.i: Then she said, 'Take for me this and that.'
sentences.n: خذلي is printed as one word, خُذْ لِي 'take for me'. كذا وكذا 'such and such' stands for a list of goods.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذْتُ لَهَا مِنَ التُّجَّارِ مَا أَرَادَتْ وَأَخَذَتْهُ وَمَضَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhtu lahā min al-tujjāri mā arādat wa-akhadhat-hu wa-maḍat
sentences.l: so I-took for-her from the-merchants what she-wanted, and she-took-it and she-went-away
sentences.i: So I took for her from the merchants whatever she wanted, and she took it and went away.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ تُخَاطِبْنِي فِي ثَمَنِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam tukhāṭibnī fī thamanihi
sentences.l: and not she-addressed-me about its-price
sentences.i: She never spoke to me about its price.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا مَضَتْ نَدِمْتُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَكُنْتُ أَخَذْتُ الَّذِي طَلَبَتْهُ بِأَلْفِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā maḍat nadimtu ʿalā dhālika wa-kuntu akhadhtu al-ladhī ṭalabathu bi-alfi dīnārin
sentences.l: so when she-went-away I-regretted upon that, and I-was I-had-taken the-which she-asked-for at a-thousand dinar
sentences.i: When she had gone I regretted it, for the goods she asked for, I had taken at a thousand dinars.
sentences.n: كنت أخذت 'I had taken' is the pluperfect (كان + perfect).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا غَابَتْ عَنْ عَيْنِي قُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ghābat ʿan ʿaynī qultu fī nafsī
sentences.l: so when she-was-absent from my-eye I-said in my-self
sentences.i: When she had vanished from my sight I said to myself:

sentences.t: أَيْشْ هَذِهِ الْمَحَبَّةُ أَعْطَتْنِي خَمْسَةَ أَلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ وَأَخَذَتْ شَيْئًا بِأَلْفِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: aysh hādhihi al-maḥabbatu aʿṭatnī khamsata ālāfi dirhamin wa-akhadhat shayʾan bi-alfi dīnārin
sentences.l: what is-this the-love? She-gave-me five thousands of-dirham, and she-took a-thing for a-thousand dinar
sentences.i: What kind of love is this? She gave me five thousand dirhams, and took goods worth a thousand dinars!
sentences.n: ايش is Middle Arabic 'what', contracted from أيّ شيء. The clause that follows is asyndetic, with no 'that' or 'since'; it explains the question.

sentences.t: فَحَسِيتُ بِالْفَقْرِ مِنْ مَالِ التُّجَّارِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥasītu bi-al-faqri min māli al-tujjāri
sentences.l: so I-felt with-the-poverty from the-wealth of-the-merchants
sentences.i: So I felt poverty creeping on me, because of the merchants' money.
sentences.n: حسيت is the Middle Arabic form of 'I felt' (Classical أحسست); the sense of 'from the merchants' money' is 'on account of what I owed them'.

sentences.t: وَقُلْتُ إِنَّ التُّجَّارَ لَمْ يَعْرِفُوا إِلَّا أَنَا
sentences.tr: wa-qultu inna al-tujjāra lam yaʿrifū illā anā
sentences.l: and I-said: indeed the-merchants have-not known except me
sentences.i: And I said: the merchants know no one but me.

sentences.t: فَمَا كَانَتْ هَذِهِ الْمَرْأَةُ إِلَّامُحْتَالَةً خَدَعَتْنِي بِحُسْنِهَا وَجَمَالِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-mā kānat hādhihi al-marʾatu illāmuḥtālatan khadaʿatnī bi-ḥusnihā wa-jamālihā
sentences.l: so not was this the-woman except a-trickster: she-deceived-me with-her-beauty and her-loveliness
sentences.i: This woman was nothing but a trickster, who deceived me with her beauty and her loveliness.
sentences.n: The print joins إلا and محتالة into one word. محتالة is predicate (accusative) after ما كانت ... إلا.

sentences.t: وَرَأَتْنِي صَغِيرًا فَضَحِكَتْ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: wa-raʾatnī ṣaghīran fa-ḍaḥikat ʿalayya
sentences.l: and she-saw-me small, so she-laughed upon-me
sentences.i: She saw I was young, and made a fool of me.
sentences.n: ضحك على 'laugh at, make a fool of'.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ أَسْأَلْهَا عَنْ مَنْزِلِهَا وَلَمْ أَزَلْ فِي وَسْوَاسٍ
sentences.tr: wa-lam asʾalhā ʿan manzilihā wa-lam azal fī waswāsin
sentences.l: and not I-asked-her about her-dwelling, and not I-ceased in an-obsession
sentences.i: I never asked her where she lived, and I remained in a fever of doubt.
sentences.n: وسواس is the whispering of worry, 'obsession, anxious brooding'.

sentences.t: وَطَالَتْ غَيْبَتُهَا أَكْثَرَ مِنْ شَهْرٍ
sentences.tr: wa-ṭālat ghaybatuhā akthara min shahrin
sentences.l: and it-grew-long her-absence, more than a-month
sentences.i: Her absence dragged on for more than a month.

sentences.t: فَطَالَبُونِي التُّجَّارُ وَشَدَّدُوا عَلَيَّ فَقَدَّمْتُ عَقَارِي لِلْمَبِيعِ وَأَضْمَرْتُ عَلَى الْهَلَاكِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṭālabūnī al-tujjāru wa-shaddadū ʿalayya fa-qaddamtu ʿaqārī li-al-mabīʿi wa-aḍmartu ʿalā al-halāki
sentences.l: so they-pressed-me, the-merchants, and they-were-severe upon-me, so I-put-forward my-property for-the-sale, and I-concealed-resolve upon the-ruin
sentences.i: The merchants pressed me again, and bore down hard on me. So I put my property up for sale, and resigned myself to ruin.
sentences.n: أضمر على 'to be secretly resolved on' is my reading; it is not common, and the sense may be 'braced myself for ruin'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَعَدَّتْ وَأَنَا مُتَفَكِّرٌ
sentences.tr: thumma taʿaddat wa-anā mutafakkirun
sentences.l: then she/it-passed-beyond, while I thinking
sentences.i: Then time passed, while I sat brooding.
sentences.n: تعدت is obscure: 'it passed on' with no stated subject. It may be corrupt for قعدت 'I sat', which would suit متفكر 'brooding'.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ أَشْعُرْ إِلَّا وَهِيَ نَازِلَةٌ عَلَى بَابِ السُّوقِ وَدَخَلَتْ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-lam ashʿur illā wa-hiya nāzilatun ʿalā bābi al-sūqi wa-dakhalat ʿalayya
sentences.l: so not I-was-aware except she dismounting at the-gate of-the-market, and she-entered upon-me
sentences.i: And I knew nothing until I saw her dismounting at the market gate; and she came in to me.
sentences.n: فلم أشعر إلا وهي 'I was not aware until there she was' is a stock turn for a sudden arrival.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَيْتُهَا زَالَتِ الْفِكْرَةُ وَنَسِيتُ مَا كُنْتُ فِيهِ وَأَقْبَلَتْ تُحَدِّثُنِي بِحَدِيثِهَا الْحَسَنِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾaytuhā zālati al-fikratu wa-nasītu mā kuntu fīhi wa-aqbalat tuḥadditunī bi-ḥadīthihā al-ḥasani
sentences.l: so when I-saw-her the-worry vanished, and I-forgot what I-was in-it, and she-approached, she-talks-to-me with-her-speech the-fair
sentences.i: When I saw her my worry vanished and I forgot the state I was in, while she began to talk to me in her sweet way.
sentences.n: أقبل + imperfect 'set about doing'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ هَاتِ الصَّيْرَفِيَّ وَأَوْزِنْ مَا لَكَ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat hāti al-ṣayrafiyya wa-awzin mā laka
sentences.l: then she-said: bring the-money-changer, and weigh what is-to-you
sentences.i: Then she said, 'Bring the money-changer, and weigh out what is owed to you.'
sentences.n: اوزن is printed unpointed; I read it as imperative of the Form IV أوزن, 'have weighed out'. Classical would be زن. Another reading is passive, 'and let what is yours be weighed'.

sentences.t: فَأَعْطَتْنِي ثَمَنَ مَا أَخَذَتْهُ بِزِيَادَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-aʿṭatnī thamana mā akhadhat-hu bi-ziyādatin
sentences.l: so she-gave-me the-price of-what she-took, with an-increase
sentences.i: So she paid me the price of what she had taken, and more besides.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ انْبَسَطَتْ مَعِي فِي الْكَلَامِ فَكِدْتُ أَمُوتُ فَرَحًا وَسُرُورًا
sentences.tr: thumma inbasaṭat maʿī fī al-kalāmi fa-kidtu amūtu faraḥan wa-surūran
sentences.l: then she-expanded with-me in the-talk, so I-nearly I-die in-gladness and in-joy
sentences.i: Then she opened up to me in conversation, and I nearly died of gladness and joy.
sentences.n: كاد + imperfect 'almost did'; فرحا وسرورا are accusatives of cause.

sentences.t: حَتَّى قَالَتْ لِى أَنْتَ لَكَ زَوْجَةٌ
sentences.tr: ḥattā qālat lī anta laka zawjatun
sentences.l: until she-said to-me: you, to-you a-wife
sentences.i: until she said to me, 'Have you a wife?'
sentences.n: The yes-or-no question has no question particle; only the tone marks it.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَا إِنِّي لَاأَعْرِفُ امْرَأَةً قَطُّ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lā innī lāaʿrifu imraʾatan qaṭṭu
sentences.l: so I-said: no, indeed-I not-I-know a-woman ever
sentences.i: I said, 'No, I have never known a woman.'
sentences.n: The print joins لا and أعرف into one word.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَكَيْتُ فَقَالَتْ لِي مَالَكَ تَبْكِي فَقُلْتُ خَيْرٌ
sentences.tr: thumma bakaytu fa-qālat lī mālaka tabkī fa-qultu khayrun
sentences.l: then I-wept, so she-said to-me: what-to-you, you-weep? so I-said: good
sentences.i: Then I wept, and she said to me, 'What is the matter with you, that you weep?' I said, 'Nothing.'
sentences.n: مالك is printed as one word, 'what is with you?'; خير 'good' is the polite brush-off, 'it is nothing'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنِّي أَخَذْتُ بَعْضَ الدَّنَانِيرِ وَأَعْطَيْتُهَا لِلْخَادِمِ وَسَأَلْتُهُ أَنْ يَتَوَسَّطَ فِي الْأَمْرِ
sentences.tr: thumma innī akhadhtu baʿḍa al-danānīri wa-aʿṭaytuhā li-al-khādimi wa-saʾaltuhu an yatawassaṭa fī al-amri
sentences.l: then indeed-I I-took some of-the-dinars, and I-gave-them to-the-servant, and I-asked-him that he-mediate in the-matter
sentences.i: Then I took some of the dinars, gave them to the servant, and begged him to intercede for me in the matter.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ وَقَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika wa-qāla
sentences.l: so he-laughed and he-said
sentences.i: He laughed and said:

sentences.t: هِيَ عَاشِقَةٌ لَكَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْكَ
sentences.tr: hiya ʿāshiqatun laka akthara minka
sentences.l: she is a-lover to-you more than-you
sentences.i: 'She is more in love with you than you are with her.
sentences.n: The thing loved is introduced by ل: عاشقة لك 'in love with you'.

sentences.t: وَمَا لَهَا بِالْقُمَاشِ الَّذِي اشْتَرَتْهُ مِنْكَ حَاجَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-mā lahā bi-al-qumāshi al-ladhī ishtarat-hu minka ḥājatun
sentences.l: and not to-her with-the-cloth which she-bought-it from-you a-need
sentences.i: She has no need at all of the cloth she bought from you.
sentences.n: حاجة بـ 'need of' takes بـ; the returning pronoun in اشترته 'bought it' is normal.

sentences.t: وَإِنَّمَا فَعَلَتْ هَذَا لِأَجْلِ مَحَبَّتِهَا لَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-innamā faʿalat hādhā li-ajli maḥabbatihā laka
sentences.l: and only she-did this for the-sake of-her-love for-you
sentences.i: She did this only for the sake of her love for you.

sentences.t: فَخَاطِبْهَا بِمَا تُرِيدُ فَإِنَّهَا لَا تُخَالِفُكَ فِيمَا تَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-khāṭibhā bi-mā turīdu fa-innahā lā tukhālifuka fī-mā taqūlu
sentences.l: so address-her with-what you-want, for indeed-she not she-opposes-you in-what you-say
sentences.i: So speak to her of whatever you wish, for she will not cross you in anything you say.'
sentences.n: خاطب بـ 'speak to (someone) about'.

sentences.t: فَرَأَتْنِي وَأَنَا أُعْطِي الْخَادِمَ الدَّنَانِيرَ فَرَجَعْتُ وَجَلَسْتُ
sentences.tr: fa-raʾatnī wa-anā uʿṭī al-khādima al-danānīra fa-rajaʿtu wa-jalastu
sentences.l: so she-saw-me while I give the-servant the-dinars, so I-returned and I-sat
sentences.i: She saw me giving the servant the dinars, so I went back and sat down.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قُلْتُ لَهَا تَصَدَّقِي عَلَى مَمْلُوكِكِ وَاسْمَحِي لَهُ فِيمَا يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: thumma qultu lahā taṣaddaqī ʿalā mamlūkiki wa-isma-ḥī lahu fī-mā yaqūlu
sentences.l: then I-said to-her: be-charitable upon your-slave, and be-lenient to-him in-what he-says
sentences.i: Then I said to her, 'Be gracious to your servant, and forgive him for what he says.'
sentences.n: The sense of تصدقي على is 'show charity to'. اسمحي له فيما يقول could also be 'allow him what he asks'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ حَدَّثْتُهَا بِمَا فِي خَاطِرِي فَأَجَابَتْ قَوْلِي
sentences.tr: thumma ḥaddathtuhā bi-mā fī khāṭirī fa-ajābat qawlī
sentences.l: then I-told-her with-what is in my-mind, so she-answered my-word
sentences.i: Then I told her what was in my heart, and she answered my plea.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لِلْخَادِمِ أَنْتَ تَأْتِي بِرِسَالَتِي
sentences.tr: wa-qālat li-al-khādimi anta taʾtī bi-risālatī
sentences.l: and she-said to-the-servant: you, you-come with-my-message
sentences.i: And she said to the servant, 'You shall carry my message.'
sentences.n: أَنْتَ تَأْتِي: the pronoun before the verb adds emphasis ('it is you who...').

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِي اعْمَلْ بِمَا يَقُولُ لَكَ الْخَادِمُ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lī iʿmal bi-mā yaqūlu laka al-khādimu ʿalayhi
sentences.l: and he-said to-me: act with-what he-says to-you the-servant, upon-him
sentences.i: And he said to me, 'Do as the servant tells you; rely on him.'
sentences.n: The masculine قال is surprising after the previous sentence (we expect وقالت لي 'she said to me'); perhaps a slip. عليه is obscure and may mean 'rely on him'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَامَتْ
sentences.tr: thumma qāmat
sentences.l: then she-rose
sentences.i: Then she rose

sentences.t: وَمَضَتْ وَقُمْتُ سَلَّمْتُ اَلتُّجَّارَ أمْوَا لَهُمْ وَحَصَلَ لَهُمْ اَلرِّبْحُ
sentences.tr: wa-maḍat wa-qumtu sallamtu al-tujjāra amwā lahum wa-ḥaṣala lahum al-ribḥu
sentences.l: And she went-away, and I rose; I handed-over to-the-merchants their-goods, and there-accrued to-them the-profit.
sentences.i: She departed, and I rose and handed the merchants their goods, and they made their profit.
sentences.n: The slice opens mid-sentence. Printed اموا لهم is one word, أموالهم, broken by a gap in the print; the glossary reads the two pieces together. The subject of the first verb (a woman who has just gone) is not stated in this fragment.

sentences.t: إِلَّا أنَا حَصَلَ لِى اَلنَّدَمُ مِنْ اِنْقِطَاعِ خَبَرِهَا عَنِّي
sentences.tr: illā anā ḥaṣala lī al-nadamu min inqiṭāʿi khabarihā ʿannī
sentences.l: Except I: there-befell to-me the-regret from the-cutting-off of-news-of-her from me.
sentences.i: Only I was seized with regret that all word of her had been cut off from me.
sentences.n: إلا أنا is an emphatic 'except that I'; the print spells لى with ى for لي (so, throughout, with فى).

sentences.t: وَلَمْ أنَمْ طُولَ لَيْلَتِي
sentences.tr: wa-lam anam ṭūla laylatī
sentences.l: And not did-I-sleep the-length-of my-night.
sentences.i: I did not sleep all night long.

sentences.t: فَمَاكَانَ إِلَّا أيَّامًا قَلَائِلَ وَجَاءَنِي خَادِمُهَا فَأكْرَمْتُهُ وَسَألْتُهُ عَنْهَا فَقَالَ إِنَّهَا مَرِيضَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-mākāna illā ayyāman qalāʾila wa-jāʾanī khādimuhā fa-akramtuhu wa-saʾaltuhu ʿanhā fa-qāla innahā marīḍatun
sentences.l: And it-was not except days few, and-there-came-to-me her-servant, and-I-honoured-him and-asked-him about-her, and-he-said: that-she sick.
sentences.i: Only a few days passed before her servant came to me. I received him honourably and asked after her, and he said, "She is ill."
sentences.n: فماكان is written as one word (fa + mā kāna). Mā kāna illā ayyāman is an idiom: 'it was only days (before...)'.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لِلْخَادِمِ اِشْرَحْ لِى أمْرَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qultu li-al-khādimi ishraḥ lī amrahā
sentences.l: And-I-said to-the-servant: Explain to-me her-affair.
sentences.i: I said to the servant, "Explain her case to me."

sentences.t: قَالَ هَذِهِ اَلصَّبِيَّهُ رَبَّتْهَا اَلسِّتُّ زُبَيْدَةُ زَوْجَةُ اَلْخَلِيفَةِ هَارُونَ اَلرَّشِيدِ وَهِيَ مِنْ جَوَارِهَا
sentences.tr: qāla hādhihi al-ṣabiyyahu rabbathā al-sittu Zubaydatu zawjatu al-khalīfati Hārūna al-Rashīdi wa-hiya min jawārihā
sentences.l: He-said: This the-girl, reared-her the-Lady Zubayda, wife-of the-caliph Hārūn al-Rashīd, and-she is from her-slave-girls.
sentences.i: He said, "This girl was reared by Lady Zubayda, wife of the caliph Hārūn al-Rashīd, and she is one of her slave-girls.
sentences.n: الصبيه is printed with final ه where Classical has ة; I vocalise the ending as -a(h) and keep the printed letter. جوارها is the plural of jāriya, normally جواريها; the print drops the yāʾ, and I vocalise the letters as printed. Al-sitt, 'the Lady', is the colloquial form of sayyida.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ اِشْتَهَتْ عَلَى سَيِّدَتِهَا اَلْخُرُوجَ وَالدُّخُولَ فَوَصَلَتْ حَتَّى صَارَتْ قَهْرَمَانَةً
sentences.tr: wa-qad ishtahat ʿalā sayyidatihā al-khurūja wa-al-dukhūla fa-waṣalat ḥattā ṣārat qahramānatan
sentences.l: And she-had craved of her-mistress the-going-out and-the-going-in, and-she-advanced until she-became a-stewardess.
sentences.i: She had begged her mistress for the freedom to go out and in, and so she rose until she became a stewardess.
sentences.n: اشتهت على is obscure: literally 'she desired upon her mistress', which I take as 'she pressed her mistress for' (the freedom of coming and going). The reading is uncertain.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا حَدَّثَتْ اَلسِّتَّ بِكَ وَسَألَتْهَا أنْ تُزَوِّجَهَا بِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā ḥaddathat al-sitta bika wa-saʾalathā an tuzawwijahā bika
sentences.l: Then that-she told the-Lady about-you, and-asked-her that she-marry-her-off to-you.
sentences.i: Then she spoke to the Lady about you and begged her to marry her to you.
sentences.n: ثم انها 'then she' (literally 'then, indeed she'). The servant is speaking to the narrator, hence 'you'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ اَلسِّتُّ لَا أفْعَلُ حَتَّى أنْظُرَ هَذَا اَلشَّابَّ فَإِنْ كَانَ يُشْبِهُكِ زَوَّجْتُكِ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat al-sittu lā afʿalu ḥattā anẓura hādhā al-shābba fa-in kāna yushbihuki zawwajtuki bihi
sentences.l: And-she-said, the-Lady: Not I-do until I-see this the-young-man; and-if he-was resembling-you, I-married-you to-him.
sentences.i: And the Lady said, 'I will do nothing until I see this young man; and if he is a match for you, I will marry you to him.
sentences.n: Unpointed print does not mark gender: the Lady is speaking to the girl, so I read -ki (you, f.) in يشبهك and زوجتك, but the pointing is ours and -ka is also possible, and the youth is certainly addressed from the next unit on. Fa-in kāna ... zawwajtu: a perfect in the main clause of a condition, 'I shall marry'.

sentences.t: وَنَحْنُ نُرِيدُ اَلسَّاعَةَ نَدْخُلُ بِكَ اَلدَّارَ
sentences.tr: wa-naḥnu nurīdu al-sāʿata nadkhulu bika al-dāra
sentences.l: And-we want the-hour we-enter with-you the-house.
sentences.i: And now we mean to take you into the house.
sentences.n: Nurīdu nadkhulu with no 'an between the two verbs is a Middle Arabic feature (two imperfects side by side). The speech now turns to the youth.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ دَخَلْتَ اَلدَّارَ وَصَّلْتُ تَزْوِيجَكَ إِيَّاهَا وَإِنْ كُشِفَ أمْرُكَ ضَرَبْتُ رَقَبَتَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-in dakhalta al-dāra waṣṣaltu tazwījaka iyyāhā wa-in kushifa amruka ḍarabtu raqabataka
sentences.l: And-if you-entered the-house, I-brought-through your-marrying-off her; and-if was-uncovered your-affair, I-struck your-neck.
sentences.i: If you enter the house, I will carry through your marriage to her; but if your secret is discovered, I will strike off your head.
sentences.n: Both clauses put the perfect where English wants a future (condition and result). وصلت is unclear: I read waṣṣaltu (II, 'I shall bring through'), but waṣaltu is possible.

sentences.t: فَمَا ذَاتَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-mā dhātaqūlu
sentences.l: So what say-you?
sentences.i: So what do you say?'"
sentences.n: ذاتقول is printed as one word, for mā dhā taqūlu, 'what do you say?'. The servant's reported speech ends here.

sentences.t: قُلْتُ لَهُمْ أرُوحُ مَعَكَ وَأصْبِرُ عَلَى اَلْأمْرِ اَلَّذِي حَدَّثْتَنِي بِهِ
sentences.tr: qultu lahum arūḥu maʿaka wa-aṣbiru ʿalā al-amri alladhī ḥaddathtanī bihi
sentences.l: I-said to-them: I-go with-you and-I-am-patient over the-matter which you-told-me of-it.
sentences.i: I said, "I will go with you, and I will bear with whatever you have told me."
sentences.n: لهم 'to them' is plural although only the servant has spoken, and the words that follow are addressed to him (معك): the print loosely includes the Lady's household. Aruḥu with no 'an: see the note on nurīdu nadkhulu.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ اَلْخَادِمُ إِذَا كَانَ هَذِهِ اَللَّيْلَةَ فَامْضِ إِلَى اَلْمَسْجِدِ وَصَلِّ فِيهِ وَبِتْ فِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-khādimu idhā kāna hādhihi al-layla fa-imḍi ilā al-masjidi wa-ṣalli fīhi wa-bit fīhi
sentences.l: And-he-said to-him, the-servant: When it-was this the-night, then-go to the-mosque and-pray in-it and-spend-the-night in-it.
sentences.i: The servant said to him, "When tonight comes, go to the mosque, pray in it and pass the night there.
sentences.n: The narrator slips from 'I' into the third person ('said to him'). Idhā kāna ... with an accusative 'this night' is idiomatic: 'when it is this night', that is, 'tonight'. Hādhihi al-layla is left unpointed for case by the print; I read it as an accusative of time.

sentences.t: وَهَذَا اَلْمَسْجِدُ اَلَّذِي بَنَتْهُ اَلسِّتُّ زُبَيْدَةُ عَلَى اَلْلَ جَلَة
sentences.tr: wa-hādhā al-masjidu alladhī banathu al-sittu Zubaydatu ʿalā al-la jala
sentences.l: And this the-mosque which built-it the-Lady Zubayda upon al-l jala.
sentences.i: This is the mosque that Lady Zubayda built on the Tigris."
sentences.n: الل جلة is printed as two pieces and I cannot read them as ordinary words. The likeliest intention is الدجلة, 'the Tigris' (Dijla), with a lām for dāl and a stray space; I vocalise the letters as printed and offer this only as a candidate.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ حُبًّا وَكَرَامَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qultu ḥubban wa-karāmatan
sentences.l: And-I-said: Love and-honour.
sentences.i: I said, "Gladly, and with honour."
sentences.n: Ḥubban wa-karāmatan, 'with love and honour', is the stock formula for willing consent.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّاكَانَ اَلْعِشَاءُ مَضَيْتُ اِى اَلْمَسْجِدِ وَصَلَّيْتُ فِيهِ وَبِتُّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammākāna al-ʿishāʾu maḍaytu ilā al-masjidi wa-ṣallaytu fīhi wa-bittu
sentences.l: And-when it-was the-evening I-went to the-mosque, and-I-prayed in-it and-I-spent-the-night.
sentences.i: When evening came I went to the mosque, prayed there and stayed the night.
sentences.n: Printed اى stands for إلى (the lām is missing) and فلماكان is one word; I vocalise the letters printed and read 'ilā'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ وَقْتُ اَلسَّحَرِ وَإِذَا بِخَادِمَيْنِ أقْبَلَا فِي زَوْرَقٍ وَمَعَهُمَا صَنَادِيقُ فَارِغَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna waqtu al-saḥari wa-idhā bi-khādimayni aqbalā fī zawraqin wa-maʿahumā ṣanādīqu fārighatun
sentences.l: And-when it-was the-time of-the-pre-dawn, and-behold, two-servants approached in a-boat, and-with-them-two chests empty.
sentences.i: And when it was the hour before dawn, behold, two servants came up in a boat, with empty chests.
sentences.n: Wa-idhā bi- marks a sudden appearance: 'and behold, (there were) two servants'. The feminine singular فارغة agrees with a plural of things, as is normal.

sentences.t: فَأدْخَلُوهَا اَلْمَسْجِدَ وَانْصَرَفُوا وَتَأخَّرَ وَاحِدٌ مِنْهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-adkhalūhā al-masjida wa-inṣarafū wa-taʾakhkhara wāḥidun minhum
sentences.l: And-they-brought-them-in the-mosque, and-they-went-away, and-lagged one of-them.
sentences.i: They carried them into the mosque and went away, but one of them stayed behind.

sentences.t: فَتَأمَّلْتُهُ فَإِذَا هُوَ اَلَّذِي كَانَ وَاسِطَةً بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-taʾammaltuhu fa-idhā huwa alladhī kāna wāsiṭatan baynī wa-baynahā
sentences.l: And-I-scrutinised-him, and-behold he the-one-who was an-intermediary between-me and-between-her.
sentences.i: I looked closely at him, and behold, he was the one who had been the go-between for her and me.

sentences.t: فَبَعْدَ سَاعَةٍ صَعِدَتْ إِلَيْنَا اَلْجَارِيَةُ صَاحِبَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-baʿda sāʿatin ṣaʿidat ilaynā al-jāriyatu ṣāḥibatī
sentences.l: And-after an-hour came-up to-us the-girl, my-companion.
sentences.i: After an hour the girl, my companion, came up to us.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أقْبَلَتْ قُمْتُ إِلَيْهَا وَعَانَقْتُهَا فَقَبَّلَتْنِي وَبَكَتْ وَتَحَدَّثْنَا سَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aqbalat qumtu ilayhā wa-ʿānaqtuhā fa-qabbalatnī wa-bakat wa-taḥaddathnā sāʿatan
sentences.l: And-when she-approached I-rose to-her and-embraced-her, and-she-kissed-me and-wept, and-we-conversed an-hour.
sentences.i: When she came near I rose to her and embraced her; she kissed me and wept, and we talked for an hour.

sentences.t: فَأخَذَتْنِي وَوَضَعَتْنِي فِي صُنْدُوقٍ وَأغْلَقَتْهُ عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhatnī wa-waḍaʿatnī fī ṣundūqin wa-aghlaqathu ʿalayya
sentences.l: And-she-took-me and-put-me in a-chest and-shut-it upon me.
sentences.i: Then she took me, put me in a chest, and shut it over me.

sentences.t: وَأقْبَلَتْ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى اَلْخَادِمِ وَمَعَهُ شَئٌْ كَثِيرٌ مِنْ اَلْأمْتِعَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-aqbalat baʿda dhālika ʿalā al-khādimi wa-maʿahu shayʾun kathīrun min al-amtiʿati
sentences.l: And-she-turned after that to the-servant, and-with-him a-thing much of the-goods.
sentences.i: After that she turned to the servant, who had with him a great quantity of goods.
sentences.n: Printed شي is شيء with its hamza left out.

sentences.t: وَجَعَلَتْ تَأخُذُ وَتُعَبِّي فِي هَذِهِ اَلصَّنَادِيقِ وَتُغْلِقُ وَاحِدًا بَعْدَ وَاحِدٍ
sentences.tr: wa-jaʿalat taʾkhudhu wa-tuʿabbī fī hādhihi al-ṣanādīqi wa-tughliqu wāḥidan baʿda wāḥidin
sentences.l: And-she-began she-takes and-packs in these the-chests and-closes one after one.
sentences.i: She began to take things and pack them into these chests, shutting one after another.
sentences.n: Jaʿala with an imperfect is the 'began to' construction. تعبي is a Middle Arabic yāʾ-form of Classical تعبّئ (ʿabbaʾa, 'to pack'); the print has no hamza.

sentences.t: حَتَّى عَبَّتِ اَلْجَمِيعَ ثُمَّ وَضَعُوهُمْ فِى اَلزَّوْرَقِ وَأخَذُوا طَالِبِينَ مَنْزِلَ
sentences.tr: ḥattā ʿabbati al-jamīʿa thumma waḍaʿūhum fī al-zawraqi wa-akhadhū ṭālibīna manzila
sentences.l: Until she-had-packed the-whole; then they-put-them in the-boat, and-they-set-off seeking the-abode of
sentences.i: until she had packed it all. Then they put them in the boat and set off, making for the dwelling of
sentences.n: The slice ends mid-sentence: manzila is the first term of a genitive construction completed in the next slice. عبت is the perfect ʿabba(ʾa)t, spelled without hamza or yāʾ; the final kasra of ʿabbati is the linking vowel before al-. Waḍaʿūhum has a masculine plural suffix for the chests; the narrator now says 'they' of the servants.

sentences.t: اَلسِّتِّ زُبَيْدَةَ
sentences.tr: al-sitti Zubaydata
sentences.l: the-Lady Zubayda
sentences.i: Lady Zubayda
sentences.n: A fragment: the unit begins mid-sentence, so the case ending (genitive here) is a guess. سِتّ is colloquial 'lady' (for Classical sayyida), a Middle Arabic feature you will meet often.

sentences.t: فَلَحِقَنِي الْفِكْرُ وَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي لَقَدْ هَلَكْتُ مِنْ أَجْلِ شَهْوَتِي وَهَلْ تَحْصُلُ أَوْلَا
sentences.tr: fa-laḥiqanī al-fikru wa-qultu fī nafsī la-qad halaktu min ajli shahwatī wa-hal taḥṣulu aw lā
sentences.l: so there-overtook-me the-thought, and I-said in my-self: 'indeed I-have-perished on-account-of my-lust, and whether it-will-be-attained or not'
sentences.i: Then a thought overtook me, and I said to myself, 'I am lost, ruined by my own desire, and who knows whether I shall even obtain it?'
sentences.n: The printed اولا is read as أَوْ لَا, 'or not', completing 'whether it will come about or not'.

sentences.t: وَجَعَلْتُ أَبْكِي وَأَنَا فِى الصُّنْدُوقِ وَأَدْعُو اللَّهَ أَنْ يُخَلِّصَنِي مِمَّا أَنَا فِيهِ
sentences.tr: wa-jaʿaltu abkī wa-anā fī al-ṣundūqi wa-adʿū Allāha an yukhalliṣanī mimmā anā fīhi
sentences.l: and I-began I-weep, while-I in the-chest, and I-call-upon God that he-deliver-me from-what I in-it
sentences.i: And I began to weep inside the chest, praying God to deliver me from my plight.
sentences.n: جَعَلَ followed by a present verb means 'began to'. مِمَّا is مِنْ + مَا, 'from that which'.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا سَائِرِينَ حَتَّى وَصَلُوا بِالصَّنَادِيقِ عَلَى بَابِ الْخَلِيفَةِ وَحَمَلُوا الصُّنْدُوقَ الَّذِى أَنَا فِيهِ مِنْ جُمْلَتِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazālū sāʾirīna ḥattā waṣalū bi-al-ṣanādīqi ʿalā bābi al-khalīfati wa-ḥamalū al-ṣundūqa alladhī anā fīhi min jumlatihim
sentences.l: and-not they-ceased walking, until they-arrived with-the-chests at the-door of-the-caliph, and they-carried the-chest which I in-it from their-totality
sentences.i: They went on walking until they reached the Caliph's gate with the chests, and they lifted the chest I was in along with all the rest.
sentences.n: وَصَلَ بِـ is 'arrive bringing'. مِنْ جُمْلَتِهِمْ, 'from their totality', means 'among the whole lot of them'. Note سائرين is accusative, the usual predicate after لَمْ يَزَالُوا.

sentences.t: فَاجْتَازَتْ طَائِفَةٌ مِنَ الْخُدَّامِ الْمُوَكَّلِينَ بِالْحَرِيمِ وَأَصْحَابِ السَّتَائِرِ إِلَى أَنْ أَتَوْا إِلَى خَادِمٍ كَبِيرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ajtāzat ṭāʾifatun min al-khuddāmi al-muwakkalīna bi-al-ḥarīmi wa-aṣḥābi al-satāʾiri ilā an atawā ilā khādimin kabīrin
sentences.l: so there-passed a-company of the-servants the-entrusted-ones with-the-harem and the-owners of-the-curtains, until they-came to a-servant great
sentences.i: A company of the servants set over the harem, and the keepers of the curtains, passed by, until they came to a senior eunuch.
sentences.n: خادم 'servant' is the usual word for a palace eunuch; 'owners of the curtains' are the doorkeepers who draw the harem curtains. الموكلين is a passive participle, 'those entrusted with', and takes بِـ for the thing entrusted.

sentences.t: فَانْتَبَهَ مِنَ النَّوْمِ وَصَاحَ عَلَيْهَا وَقَالَ لَهَا أَيْشْ فِي هَذِهِ الصَّنَادِيقِ
sentences.tr: fa-intabaha min al-nawmi wa-ṣāḥa ʿalayhā wa-qāla lahā aysh fī hādhihi al-ṣanādīqi
sentences.l: so he-woke from the-sleep, and he-cried at-her, and he-said to-her: 'what-thing in these the-chests'
sentences.i: He woke from his sleep, shouted at her, and said, 'What is in these chests?'
sentences.n: ايش is the colloquial contraction of أَيُّ شَيْءٍ, 'what?'; it recurs below. صَاحَ عَلَى is 'shout at'.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ مَلْأَنِينَ أَمْتِعَةً لِلسِّتِّ زُبَيْدَةَ
sentences.tr: qālat malʾanīna amtiʿatan li-al-sitti Zubaydata
sentences.l: she-said: 'full-ones of-goods for-the-Lady Zubayda'
sentences.i: She said, 'They are full of goods for Lady Zubayda.'
sentences.n: ملأنين is a Middle Arabic sound plural of مَلْآن 'full' (Classical would use مَلِيئَة or مَمْلُوءَة). Printed without a connecting فَـ, as often in reported dialogue.

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهَا افْتَحِي وَاحِدٌ! وَاحِدًا حَتَّى أَنْظُرَ أَيْشْ فِيهِمْ
sentences.tr: qāla lahā iftaḥī wāḥidan! wāḥidan ḥattā anẓura aysh fīhim
sentences.l: he-said to-her: 'open one! one, until I-look what-thing in-them'
sentences.i: 'Open them one by one,' he said, 'until I see what is in them.'
sentences.n: The exclamation mark after the first واحد is in the print (probably a misprint for the alif of واحدا); it is kept as printed, and the first word is pointed as printed, without the alif. Repeating a word gives 'one by one'. The sense of the verb حتى + subjunctive is 'until/so that'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِأَيِّ شَيْ تَفْتَحُهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat li-ayyi shayʾ taftaḥuhum
sentences.l: so she-said: 'for which thing do-you-open them'
sentences.i: She said, 'Why should you open them?'
sentences.n: شي is the shortened colloquial spelling of شَيْء 'thing'; لِأَيِّ شَيْءٍ 'for what thing' means 'why'.

sentences.t: فَصَاحَ عَلَيْهَا وَقَالَ لَاتُطِيلِي لَا بُدَّ مِنْ فَتْحِ هَذِهِ الصَّنَادِيقِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāḥa ʿalayhā wa-qāla lā tuṭīlī lā budda min fatḥi hādhihi al-ṣanādīqi
sentences.l: so he-cried at-her and he-said: 'do-not-prolong; no escape from the-opening of-these the-chests'
sentences.i: He shouted at her, 'Don't drag it out! These chests must be opened.'
sentences.n: The print joins لاتطيلي into one word, 'do not prolong' (the talk). لَا بُدَّ مِنْ, 'there is no escape from', means 'it must be'.

sentences.t: وَقَامَ قَائِمًا
sentences.tr: wa-qāma qāʾiman
sentences.l: and he-rose standing
sentences.i: And he rose to his feet.
sentences.n: قائما 'standing' is an accusative state-clause (hāl) describing how he rose.

sentences.t: فَأَوَّلُ مَا بَدَأَ بِفَتْحِ الصُّنْدُوقِ الَّذِي أَنَا فِيهِ فَقَدْ مَوَالِي لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-awwalu mā badaʾa bi-fatḥi al-ṣundūqi alladhī anā fīhi fa-qad mawālī lahu
sentences.l: so the-first [thing] that he-began with-the-opening of-the-chest which I in-it: then-indeed my-masters to-him
sentences.i: The first chest he began to open was the one I was in.
sentences.n: The last three words, فقد موالي له, are obscure and possibly corrupt. One candidate reading is فَقَدْ مَوَالِي لَهُ 'and indeed my patrons were his'; another is a slip for a verb such as فَقَدَّ or a damaged phrase. The next sentence shows that terror struck me then, so the idiomatic line gives only the clear part. بَدَأَ بِـ is 'begin with'.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ زَالَ عَقْلِي وَبُلْتُ عَلَى نَفْسِي مِنْ خَوْفِي وَخَرَجَ بَوْلِى مِنْ خَارِجِ الصُّنْدُوقِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika zāla ʿaqlī wa-bultu ʿalā nafsī min khawfī wa-kharaja bawlī min khāriji al-ṣundūqi
sentences.l: so at that my-reason departed, and I-urinated upon myself from my-fear, and my-urine went-out from the-outside of-the-chest
sentences.i: At that my wits left me, I wet myself in terror, and my urine ran out of the chest.
sentences.n: The text is frank here and so is the translation. من خارج الصندوق, 'from the outside of the chest', has the urine showing outside it.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِلْمُقَدَّمِ يَا مُقَدَّمُ أَهْلَكْتَنِي وَأَهْلَكْتَ نَفْسَكَ وَأَفْسَدْتَ شَيْئًا يُسَاوِي عَشَرَةَ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat li-al-muqaddami yā muqaddamu ahlaktanī wa-ahlakta nafsaka wa-afsadta shayʾan yusāwī ʿasharata ālāfi dīnārin
sentences.l: so she-said to-the-foremost: 'O foremost! you-destroyed-me and you-destroyed yourself and you-spoiled a-thing equalling ten of-thousands of-dinar'
sentences.i: She said to the chief, 'Chief, you have ruined me and ruined yourself, and spoiled goods worth ten thousand dinars!'
sentences.n: المقدم, 'the one put in front', is the commander of the eunuchs, the senior of the guard. نفسك 'your self' is the ordinary way to say 'yourself'.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ فِي هَذَا الصُّنْدُوقِ ثِيَابٌ مُلَوَّنَاتٌ وَأَرْبَعَةَ أَمْنَانٍ مِنْ مَاءِ زَمْزَمَ
sentences.tr: fa-inna fī hādhā al-ṣundūqi thiyābun mulawwanātun wa-arbaʿata amnānin min māʾi zamzama
sentences.l: for indeed in this the-chest [are] garments coloured, and four maunds of water of-Zamzam
sentences.i: For in this chest are coloured garments and four maunds of Zamzam water.
sentences.n: The print has ثياب ملونات without the accusative alif, so they are pointed as nominative, as Middle Arabic often does after إنّ with a fronted predicate. The maund (مَنّ, plural أمنان) is a measure of weight, about two pounds. Zamzam is the sacred well at Mecca, whose water is prized.

sentences.t: وَهَذِهِ السَّاعَةَ انْفَكَّتْ وَجَرَتْ عَلَى الثِّيَابِ الَّتِي فِى الصُّنْدُوقِ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhihi al-sāʿata infakkat wa-jarat ʿalā al-thiyābi allatī fī al-ṣundūqi
sentences.l: and this the-hour it-came-undone and ran over the-garments which in the-chest
sentences.i: And just now it has come undone and run over the clothes in the chest,
sentences.n: هذه الساعة, 'this hour', is the adverb 'just now'. The subject of انفكت (the water, or its container) is left unstated.

sentences.t: وَالسَّاعَةَ تَنْفَسِخُ أَلْوَ انُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-al-sāʿata tanfasikhu alwa ānuhā
sentences.l: and the-hour will-be-undone their-colours
sentences.i: and any moment now their colours will be ruined.
sentences.n: The print splits ألوانها 'their colours' into الو انها, a word-division slip; the pointing keeps the split. تنفسخ 'be undone, dissolve' is taken to mean the dyes running.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا الطَّوَا شِي خُذِي صَنَادِيقَكِ وَاذْ هَبِى إِلَى لَعْنَةِ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā al-ṭawā shī khudhī ṣanādīqaki wa-idh habī ilā laʿnati Allāhi
sentences.l: so he-said to-her, the-eunuch: 'take your-chests and go to the-curse of-God'
sentences.i: The eunuch said to her, 'Take your chests and go to perdition!'
sentences.n: The print splits الطواشي (ṭawāshī, a eunuch of rank) as الطوا شي and واذهبي as واذ هبى; the pointing keeps both splits. 'Go to the curse of God' is a rude dismissal.

sentences.t: فَحَمَلَتِ الْخُدَّامُ صُنْدُوقِي وَأَسْرَعُوا وَتَلَا حَقَتِ الصَّنَادِيقُ بِصُنْدُوقِي
sentences.tr: fa-ḥamalati al-khuddāmu ṣundūqī wa-asraʿū wa-talā ḥaqati al-ṣanādīqu bi-ṣundūqī
sentences.l: so carried the-servants my-chest, and they-hurried, and followed-one-another the-chests with my-chest
sentences.i: The servants picked up my chest and hurried off, and the other chests closed up behind mine.
sentences.n: Feminine singular حَمَلَتْ with the plural collective الخدام is common in this register. تلا حقت is a printed split of تلاحقت 'followed close upon one another'; the pointing keeps the split.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ ذَاهِبِينَ وَإِذَا جَاءَ فِي أُذُنِي قَائِلًا يَقُولُ وَيْلَاهُ وَيْلَاهُ الْخَلِيفَةَ الْخَلِيفَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā hum dhāhibīna wa-idhā jāʾa fī udhunī qāʾilan yaqūlu waylāhu waylāhu al-khalīfata al-khalīfata
sentences.l: so between-what they going, and-behold there-came in my-ear a-sayer saying: 'woe-to-him, woe-to-him! the-caliph! the-caliph!'
sentences.i: While they were walking along, someone came and said in my ear, 'Alas, alas! The Caliph! The Caliph!'
sentences.n: بينما ... وإذا is the Middle Arabic pairing (Classical drops the و). ذاهبين is accusative where Classical has ذاهبون. The subject of جاء is not stated. ويلاه is an exclamation of alarm; الخليفة is the warning accusative, 'beware the Caliph'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ ذَلِكَ مُتُّ فِي جِلْدِي وَقُلْتُ كَلِمَةً لَا يَخْجَلُ قَائِلُهَا لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu dhālika muttu fī jildī wa-qultu kalimatan lā yakhjalu qāʾiluhā lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-Allāhi al-ʿaliyyi al-ʿaẓīmi
sentences.l: so when I-heard that I-died in my-skin, and I-said a-word whose-sayer is-not-ashamed: 'no power and no strength except by-God the-High the-Mighty'
sentences.i: When I heard that, I died inside my own skin, and I spoke words that shame no one who says them: 'There is no power and no strength except through God, the High, the Almighty.'
sentences.n: مُتُّ فِي جِلْدِي, 'I died in my skin', means 'I nearly died of fright'. The formula لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله is the Muslim phrase of resignation; بِـ here means 'by means of'.

sentences.t: هَذِهِ مُصِيبَةٌ عَمِلْتُهَا بِنَفْسِي
sentences.tr: hādhihi muṣībatun ʿamiltuhā bi-nafsī
sentences.l: this a-calamity I-did-it with-myself
sentences.i: This is a calamity I have brought on myself.
sentences.n: A continuation of the speech with no introducing verb. بِنَفْسِي 'by myself' is the agent: I did it with my own self.

sentences.t: فَسَمِعْتُ الْخَلِيفَةَ يَقُولُ لِلْجَارِيَةِ صَاحِبَتِي وَيْلَكِ أَيْشْ فِي صَنَادِيقِكِ هَذِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-samiʿtu al-khalīfata yaqūlu li-al-jāriyati ṣāḥibatī waylaki aysh fī ṣanādīqiki hādhihi
sentences.l: so I-heard the-caliph saying to-the-girl, my-companion: 'woe-to-you, what-thing in your-chests these'
sentences.i: Then I heard the Caliph say to the girl, my companion, 'Woe to you! What is in these chests of yours?'
sentences.n: جارية is a slave-girl. ويلك 'woe to you' is a rebuke rather than a curse.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ فِي صَنَادِيقِي ثِيَابُ السِّتِّ زُبَيْدَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat fī ṣanādīqī thiyābu al-sitti zubaydata
sentences.l: so she-said: 'in my-chests [are] garments of-the-Lady Zubayda'
sentences.i: 'In my chests are Lady Zubayda's clothes,' she said.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ افْتَحِي لِي إِيَّاهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla iftaḥī lī iyyāhum
sentences.l: so he-said: 'open for-me them'
sentences.i: 'Open them for me,' he said.
sentences.n: إياهم is the detached object pronoun 'them', placed after the verb for emphasis.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ ذَلِكَ مُتُّ الْمَوْتَةَ الْكَامِلَةَ وَقُلْتُ فِي نَفْسِي وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ هَذَا الْيَوْمَ آخِرُ أَيَّامِي مِنَ الدُّنْيَا وَإِنْ سَلِمْتُ مِنْ هَذِهِ فَأَنَا أَتَزَوَّجُ بِهَا وَلَا كَلَامَ وَإِنِ انْكَشَفَ أَمْرِي ضُرِبَتْ رَقَبَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtu dhālika muttu al-mawtata al-kāmilata wa-qultu fī nafsī wa-Allāhi inna hādhā al-yawma ākhiru ayyāmī min al-dunyā wa-in salimtu min hādhihi fa-anā atazawwaju bihā wa-lā kalāma wa-ini inkashafa amrī ḍuribat raqabatī
sentences.l: so when I-heard that I-died the-death the-complete, and I-said in my-self: 'by-God indeed this the-day [is] last of-my-days from the-world, and if I-am-safe from this, then-I I-marry with-her, and no talk; and if my-affair is-uncovered, was-struck my-neck'
sentences.i: When I heard that, I died the whole death, and I said to myself, 'By God, this day is the last of my days in the world! If I come safe out of this, I shall marry her, and no more talk; but if my affair is uncovered, my neck will be struck.'
sentences.n: اتزوج بها uses بِـ after 'marry', where Classical takes a direct object. The past-tense ضربت is a conditional result ('will be struck'); it must be passive, ضُرِبَتْ, since the neck is the subject. وَاللَّهِ is the oath 'by God'.

sentences.t: وَجَعَلْتُ أَقُولُ أَشْهَدُأَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدً ارَسُولُ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: wa-jaʿaltu aqūlu ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāhu wa-anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāhi
sentences.l: and I-began I-say: 'I-testify that no god except God, and that Muḥammad [is] messenger of-God'
sentences.i: and I began to say, 'I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God.'
sentences.n: The print joins اشهدان (ashhadu ʾan) and prints محمد ارسول, where the stray alif is the tanwin-alif of محمدا displaced onto the next word; read it as مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ. This is the Muslim profession of faith, the shahāda, recited when death seems near.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: and overtook Shahrazād the-morning [al-ṣabāḥ], so she-fell-silent from the-speech the-permitted [al-mubāḥ]
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula of each night; ṣabāḥ and mubāḥ rhyme (sajʿ). 'Permitted speech' means the storytelling she may lawfully go on with the next night.
